title: x86-64 Interrupt Descriptor Table (IDT) entry
summary: An x86-64 IDT entry is 16 bytes (128 bits). Fields: offset (64-bit, split into low 16, middle 16, high 32), segment selector (16 bits), IST (Interrupt Stack Table, 3 bits), reserved (5 bits), type/attributes (8 bits: gate type, DPL, present), reserved (32 bits). Gate types: 0xE = interrupt gate, 0xF = trap gate, 0x5 = task gate (legacy).

structure.meaning: Low 16 bits of the handler address.
Code segment selector for the handler.
Interrupt Stack Table index (0 = use current stack, 1-7 = IST entry).
0xE = interrupt gate (IF cleared on entry), 0xF = trap gate (IF unchanged), 0x5 = task gate (legacy).
Descriptor Privilege Level (0-3). Ring level required to invoke via INT instruction.

ext.example_decoded: x86-64 IDT entry: all zeros (invalid/not present)
notes: The IDT is loaded via LIDT instruction (points to IDTR).
256 entries (0-255): 0-31 are exceptions (divide error, page fault, etc.), 32-255 are interrupts.
Interrupt gate clears IF (disables interrupts) on entry; trap gate does not.
IST (Interrupt Stack Table) provides dedicated stacks for critical handlers (double fault, NMI, machine check).

Exceptions: 0 #DE (divide error), 1 #DB (debug), 2 NMI, 3 #BP (breakpoint), 4 #OF (overflow), 5 #BR (bound range), 6 #UD (invalid opcode), 7 #NM (device not available), 8 #DF (double fault), 10 #TS (invalid TSS), 11 #NP (segment not present), 12 #SS (stack segment fault), 13 #GP (general protection), 14 #PF (page fault), 16 #MF (x87 FPU error), 17 #AC (alignment check), 18 #MC (machine check), 19 #XM (SIMD exception).
